items.name: ai-gateway
items.label: An AI app calls the gateway; Firewall filters the request, the AI Gateway function checks the key, and the call goes to a model on AI Inference, with third-party providers as the fallback

items.name: ai-gateway-latency-routing
items.label: An AI app sends real-time tasks to Mistral 3 Small on AI Inference, under 30 ms, and other tasks to OpenAI GPT-5.5

items.name: ai-gateway-model-routing
items.label: An AI app routes paid users to OpenAI GPT-5.5 with a fallback to Claude Opus 4.7, and everyone else to Kimi K2.6 or Gemma 4 depending on load

items.name: ai-gateway-provider-failover
items.label: An AI app checks whether its provider is degraded; Claude Haiku 5.5 on Anthropic is degraded, so the call falls back to Claude Haiku 5.5 on Amazon Bedrock

items.name: ai-gateway-response-cache
items.label: An AI app checks for a cached response; a match is served from the Cache API with no tokens spent, and anything else goes to a model call

items.name: ai-inference
items.label: An app reaches the application, which runs Mistral 3 Small on AI Inference in under 30 ms, pulling context from vector search on SQL Database and a fine-tuned LoRA adapter

items.name: application-accelerator
items.label: A user reaches the application; dynamic routes go through Application Accelerator to api.example.com and static assets are served from cache

items.name: applications
items.label: A user reaches the application; its rules send static assets to cache, /account to the auth-handler function and /api to the origin

items.name: bot-manager
items.label: A request crosses Firewall, which runs Bot Management; a human is allowed through and a bad bot is denied, dropped or delayed

items.name: cache
items.label: A user reaches the application, whose cache policy serves a hit from the edge cache; a miss goes to Tiered Cache and then to the origin

items.name: data-stream
items.label: Requests reach the workload; Data Stream collects HTTP, firewall and function logs and sends them through connectors to a SIEM or a data lake

items.name: ddos-protection
items.label: Users and attackers reach DDoS Protection; clean traffic is served by the workload and the flood is absorbed at the edge

items.name: edge-dns
items.label: A resolver asks the shop.example.com zone; the A record points at the workload, the MX record at the mail provider and a TXT record carries domain verification

items.name: firewall
items.label: A request reaches Firewall, whose rules apply network lists, the WAF and a rate limit in order before the storefront application runs

items.name: functions
items.label: A request matches an application rule that runs the auth-handler function; it is answered at the edge or forwarded to the origin API

items.name: image-processor
items.label: A browser asks for an image; the application runs Image Processor, which resizes and converts it, caches the variant and reads the source image from the origin once

items.name: kv-store
items.label: A request reaches the session-check function, which reads a value from the sessions namespace on KV Store at the edge and replicates writes everywhere

items.name: load-balancer
items.label: A user reaches the application; Load Balancer sends 60% of traffic to origin-a, 40% to origin-b and nothing to the unhealthy origin-c

items.name: network-shield
items.label: Traffic reaches Network Shield at the border; clean traffic goes on to the Firewall and listed ASNs, countries and IPs are dropped

items.name: object-storage
items.label: A user reaches the application, whose origin is the assets bucket on Object Storage; the object is cached at the edge and uploads come from any S3-compatible client

items.name: real-time-events
items.label: Requests reach the workload; Real-Time Events makes each one queryable in seconds, from the Console or the GraphQL API

items.name: real-time-metrics
items.label: Requests reach the workload; Real-Time Metrics reports traffic, errors and latency on dashboards and through the GraphQL API

items.name: sql-database
items.label: A request reaches the orders-api function, which queries the replicated orders database; reads hit the nearest replica and writes go to the primary

items.name: web-application-firewall
items.label: A request crosses Firewall, which runs the WAF; clean traffic goes on to the application and a threat is answered with a 403

items.name: workloads
items.label: A user reaches routing, which sends the request to the shop.example.com workload; a hit is served from cache and a miss goes to the origin

items.name: workloads-gradual-rollout
items.label: A workload splits traffic between two deployments: 10% to the new one, which is being watched, and 90% to the one that was serving

items.name: workloads-isolate-per-request
items.label: Requests reach Azion Runtime, which starts a separate isolate for each one, with no cold start

items.name: workloads-security
items.label: A user request reaches the workload over TLS, passes the bound firewall, and only then reaches the application
